hints: Express the equation in one trigonometric quantity by using $\cos x=2\cos^2(x/2)-1$.
Let $c=\cos(x/2)$, form the quadratic $4c^2-c-3=0$, and solve it.
For each admissible value of $c$, solve for $x/2$ over $0\le x/2\le\pi$.
Double the resulting angles, retain only $0\le x\le2\pi$, and give non-exact values in radians.
walkthrough:
Apply the cosine double-angle formula $\cos x = 2\cos^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - 1$ to obtain an equation in $\cos(x/2)$:
$$2\left[2\cos^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - 1\right] - \cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = 1$$

Expand and collect all terms on one side:
$$4\cos^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - 2 - \cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - 1 = 0$$
$$4\cos^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - \cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) - 3 = 0$$

Determine the interval for $\dfrac{x}{2}$:
Since $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2\pi$, the angle $\dfrac{x}{2}$ lies in the interval $0 \leqslant \dfrac{x}{2} \leqslant \pi$.

Solve the second branch $4\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 3 = 0$:
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{3}{4} = -0.75$$
In $0 \leqslant \dfrac{x}{2} \leqslant \pi$, the angle lies in the second quadrant:
$$\dfrac{x}{2} = \pi - \cos^{-1}(0.75) \approx 3.1415927 - 0.7227342 = 2.4188585 \text{ radians}$$
$$x = 2(2.4188585) \approx 4.8377 \dots \approx 4.84 \text{ radians}$$

State the solutions in the interval $0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2\pi$:
$$x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad x = 4.84$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Applies a double-angle formula to derive an equation in $\cos(x/2)$. Derives $4\cos^2(x/2)-\cos(x/2)-3=0$. The final result is $x=0$ or $x=4.84$ radians.
